behavior_evidence.interpretation_limit: Observed direction and entropy do NOT establish negative curvature or a causal next-item improvement.

candidate.effect_site: At next-item ranking after encoding the current prefix: autoregressive semantic-code token probabilities and the resulting candidate-item ranking, not the observed interaction graph or the input history encoder's available information.
candidate.euclidean_control: Use identical 32-dimensional context and code encoders, three-level 256-way semantic-ID decoder, training data, optimization, parameter count, and ranking procedure, but replace d_c with squared Euclidean distance between norm-bounded 32D vectors and logits b - ||x_h-x_{l,k}||^2/tau. Include a fixed-capacity directed-graph control with the same context/item parameter budget and directed transition inputs, but no hyperbolic distance. No control receives extra parameters, interaction history, or tuning budget.
candidate.falsifier: The hypothesis is falsified if, under the matched fixed-capacity protocol and identical held-out candidate sets, the hyperbolic model does not improve held-out Recall@K and NDCG@K over both Euclidean and directed-graph controls on the predeclared reverse-absent / higher-outdegree subset, or if any apparent gain disappears across repeated fixed seeds. It is also falsified as a curvature-specific claim if the gain is reproduced by the Euclidean control without a statistically distinguishable hyperbolic advantage.
candidate.hyperbolic_necessity: Negative curvature is motivated narrowly by the measured directional asymmetry: a shared context may need to distinguish several outgoing successor directions without making those successors mutually similar merely because they share a predecessor. Negative curvature offers greater representational volume with radius for separating branches at fixed latent dimension. The evidence does not establish branching degree distributions, hierarchy, or superiority; this is a geometry-specific hypothesis requiring a matched control.
candidate.math_definition: Use the Poincare ball of curvature -c, c>0, with dimension 32 and radius bound 1/sqrt(c). Map unconstrained vectors u to the ball by x = tanh(sqrt(c)||u||)u/(sqrt(c)||u||), with x=0 when u=0. For sequence context h and semantic-code token k at autoregressive level l, map context and token vectors to x_h and x_{l,k}; define logit z_{l,k} = b_{l,k} - d_c(x_h,x_{l,k})^2/tau, where tau>0 is a fixed temperature and d_c(x,y) = (1/sqrt(c)) arcosh(1 + 2c||x-y||^2/((1-c||x||^2)(1-c||y||^2))). Normalize logits with softmax and train by next-token cross-entropy over three semantic-ID levels (256 codes per level). Context is computed from the current interaction prefix only. The same operator is used for every code level; candidate item scores are the summed autoregressive log probabilities of their three codes.
candidate.next_item_hypothesis: In the train-only longest-prefix population, 92.66% of directed item pairs have no observed reverse event (314605/339519), so treating transitions as largely symmetric neighborhood similarity may confuse a history item's incoming and outgoing roles. Hypothesis: for next-item prediction, a fixed-dimensional negatively curved representation can better separate multiple outgoing successor directions from a shared history context, improving next-item semantic-code prediction on held-out transitions, especially for histories whose observed transitions have no reverse counterpart. This is a testable hypothesis, not evidence that the measured graph is hierarchical or that curvature is causal.
candidate.real_trigger_measurement: On a temporally held-out split, report Recall@K and NDCG@K overall and for prefix contexts whose last observed transition belongs to a pair with no reverse event in training. Also stratify by the training-measured number of distinct outgoing successors of the context item, reporting the counts per stratum; compute these strata from training only. Compare against the capacity-matched Euclidean and directed-graph controls with identical candidate sets and seeds. The claimed trigger is supported only if the target subset has enough held-out examples and the hyperbolic advantage is reproducible there.
training_only_inputs: Training interaction prefixes and next-item targets only
Semantic IDs/code assignments fitted using training items only
Training-only directed transition counts for defining reverse-absence and outgoing-successor strata
